rationale:
Evidence from iteration 4 (score 147.1, best so far): lowering base_speed from 1.4 to 1.1 more than doubled oval progress (0.32 to 0.67, one completion in 20 trials), and s-bend progress rose from 0.045 to 0.19. Speed is the main limit on the bends. Max error still sits at about 0.06 m on every track, which is the off-track limit, so the robot leaves the tape by overshoot on bends, not slow drift. Slalom is still weak at 0.11 progress with zero line losses, which points to a slow steering response on alternating bends rather than sensor dropout. Sensor geometry (spread ±0.06 m, 16 mm sensors, y 0.03 m) is working: line-loss events are near zero, so I keep it.

Changes: (1) base_speed 1.1 to 1.0, a further step down to give the bends more margin, since the speed trend is clearly positive; (2) kp 4.5 to 5.0 for a firmer correction per unit of offset, to address the slow response on slalom and the 0.06 m overshoot; (3) kd 0.6 to 0.7, a small damping increase to offset the stronger kp, kept modest because oscillation rose to 0.32 on oval; (4) ki stays at 0.3 to keep cancelling the motor mismatch. Mass, wheel track and radius are unchanged so the controller effect can be read.

Expected result: s-bend progress above 0.25, slalom progress above 0.15, and more oval completions, with max_error reaching the off-track limit less often. Oval completion time may rise slightly, but survival is worth more than speed right now.

Hypotheses for next race: (H1) if max_error still reaches 0.06 at the same bend on every trial, the steering authority is still too low and kp should go to about 6, with kd to 0.9. (H2) if steering_oscillation rises above 0.4 with kp 5.0, kd is driving chatter and should drop back to 0.5. (H3) if the robot survives on all tracks but does not finish, base_speed should rise to about 1.2 with the new gains, since finishing needs roughly 1.5 m/s average. Measurements wanted per track: completion, progress, completion_time, max_error, rms_error, line_loss_events, steering_oscillation, control_effort and noise_robustness.
